note: BH-8335. 1: bin/fly-pool.sh gives each pool machine its own route to the Fly test host at spawn and at each reuse hand-off: a Fly SSH token scoped to the test-host app only (flyctl tokens create ssh -a <TESTHOST_APP> -x <POOL_TESTHOST_TOKEN_HOURS>h), pushed mode 600 to /run/harness-env/testhost.env. bin/remote-gate.sh reads that file and reaches the host through flyctl ssh console -a <app>, so the selection gate (bin/selection-gate.sh) runs. Never an org-wide flyctl ssh issue cert. The cost is one token mint per spawn. A failure is one line in logs/fly-pool.log and the spawn goes on; the gate then records could-not-run. 0 (default): no route. Only cromford has the selection gate today, so the fleet default is 0 and the row `lane.fly-pool.cromford.pool_testhost_route` = 1 turns it on for cromford alone. A pull spawn (POOL_MACHINE_PULL) ships no route.
